summary: Jacques Leider works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne, the University of Luxembourg, and INALCO under Denise Bernot and Pierre L. Lamant. He taught at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and joined the EFEO in 2001.

Jacques May worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1981) and as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1968–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the Catholic University of Louvain and under Madeleine Biardeau at Sorbonne Nouvelle (~1972–1978). He held posts at Centre Sèvres and the Catholic University of Louvain (~1978–2007).

Jacques Soustelle was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1935) at ENS and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme, EPHE, Collège de France, and EHESS.

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Ripon, Vidyasagar, Ravenshaw, and Patna colleges, and served as dean at Banaras Hindu University and vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).

Jagdish Kashyap was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Patna College, Banaras Hindu University, and in Sri Lanka under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught at BHU and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Srikrishna Harihirlekar, Nankoo Bhaya Telang, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He served as chief producer at All India Radio and chairman of Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi.

Jake H. Davis specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Marlboro College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and CUNY, and with several traditional teachers. He held posts at Brown University, NYU, City College of New York, and BCBS.

Jakob Steiner studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and the University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen. He held professorships at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) and is Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley.
James Adam was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Atkinson was an Indologist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College.

James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under John D. Dunne and studied with numerous academic and traditional teachers, including Jan Nattier, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and the 14th Dalai Lama.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and as director and Director General (1886–1889) of the Archaeological Survey of India.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975).

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD from Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He served as a professor of law at Presidency College, Kolkata.
